# Map — tier 1, the gist

**Read this whole file, and read it before you read any source.** It is the index: what exists, and where. It is deliberately not enough to write code against.

Three ways down from here, cheapest first:

| you want | do this | costs |
|---|---|---|
| one signature | `grep -rn "#TAG:GameEntity"` — returns the definition line AND every document that cites it | nothing |
| to touch one module | open its tier-2 file: `docs/map/` + the module path with `/` and `.py` replaced by `.` + `.md`, so `scripts/core/depth.py` is [`docs/map/scripts.core.depth.md`](map/scripts.core.depth.md) | ~1 page |
| all of it | do not. Loading every tier-2 file costs more than reading the source, which is the exact failure two tiers exist to prevent | ~101k |

Generated by `tools/gen_map.py` from the AST, so no line here can name something that does not exist, and no line here has to be maintained. Regenerate after any structural edit:

    .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/gen_map.py --write

Covers `config`, `demos`, `editor`, `main.py`, `scripts`. It does **not** cover `tools/` — a check module is read whole or not at all, and the roster is generated into [`CHECKS.md`](CHECKS.md).

136 modules · 267 classes · 215 public functions · 1479 methods · 265 constants. Methods and constants are **tier 2 only** — they still carry tags, and the tag is what you grep.
